     1→/**
     2→ * OTEL-backed structured logger for the Brain server.
     3→ *
     4→ * Emits log records via the OTEL Logs API. Before initTelemetry() is called,
     5→ * the OTEL API returns a no-op logger that silently drops records.
     6→ *
     7→ * API mirrors the existing logInfo/logWarn/logError/logDebug shape from
     8→ * http/observability.ts for straightforward migration.
     9→ */
    10→
    11→import { logs, SeverityNumber } from "@opentelemetry/api-logs";
    12→
    13→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    14→// serializeError — moved from logging.ts
    15→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    16→
    17→export function serializeError(error: unknown, depth = 0): Record<string, unknown> | unknown {
    18→  if (depth > 2) {
    19→    return { message: "max depth reached" };
    20→  }
    21→
    22→  if (!(error instanceof Error)) {
    23→    return error;
    24→  }
    25→
    26→  const candidate = error as Error & {
    27→    cause?: unknown;
    28→    statusCode?: unknown;
    29→    url?: unknown;
    30→    code?: unknown;
    31→    isRetryable?: unknown;
    32→    responseHeaders?: unknown;
    33→    responseBody?: unknown;
    34→    requestBodyValues?: unknown;
    35→    data?: unknown;
    36→  };
    37→
    38→  const serialized: Record<string, unknown> = {
    39→    name: candidate.name,
    40→    message: candidate.message,
    41→    stack: candidate.stack,
    42→  };
    43→
    44→  if (candidate.statusCode !== undefined) serialized.statusCode = candidate.statusCode;
    45→  if (candidate.url !== undefined) serialized.url = candidate.url;
    46→  if (candidate.code !== undefined) serialized.code = candidate.code;
    47→  if (candidate.isRetryable !== undefined) serialized.isRetryable = candidate.isRetryable;
    48→  if (candidate.cause !== undefined) serialized.cause = serializeError(candidate.cause, depth + 1);
    49→
    50→  return serialized;
    51→}
    52→
    53→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    54→// Severity mapping
    55→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    56→
    57→interface SeverityInfo {
    58→  readonly number: SeverityNumber;
    59→  readonly text: string;
    60→}
    61→
    62→const SEVERITY_DEBUG: SeverityInfo = { number: SeverityNumber.DEBUG, text: "DEBUG" };
    63→const SEVERITY_INFO: SeverityInfo = { number: SeverityNumber.INFO, text: "INFO" };
    64→const SEVERITY_WARN: SeverityInfo = { number: SeverityNumber.WARN, text: "WARN" };
    65→const SEVERITY_ERROR: SeverityInfo = { number: SeverityNumber.ERROR, text: "ERROR" };
    66→
    67→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    68→// Core emit function
    69→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    70→
    71→function emitLogRecord(
    72→  severity: SeverityInfo,
    73→  event: string,
    74→  message: string,
    75→  meta?: Record<string, unknown>,
    76→  error?: unknown,
    77→): void {
    78→  const logger = logs.getLogger("brain-server");
    79→
    80→  const attributes: Record<string, unknown> = { event, ...meta };
    81→
    82→  if (error !== undefined) {
    83→    const serialized = serializeError(error);
    84→    if (typeof serialized === "object" && serialized !== undefined) {
    85→      const errorRecord = serialized as Record<string, unknown>;
    86→      if (errorRecord.name !== undefined) attributes["error.name"] = errorRecord.name;
    87→      if (errorRecord.message !== undefined) attributes["error.message"] = errorRecord.message;
    88→      if (errorRecord.stack !== undefined) attributes["error.stack"] = errorRecord.stack;
    89→    }
    90→  }
    91→
    92→  logger.emit({
    93→    severityNumber: severity.number,
    94→    severityText: severity.text,
    95→    body: message,
    96→    attributes,
    97→  });
    98→}
    99→
   100→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   101→// Public API — matches existing logInfo/logWarn/logError/logDebug shape
   102→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   103→
   104→export const log = {

   106→    emitLogRecord(SEVERITY_DEBUG, event, message, meta);
   107→  },
   108→
   109→  info(event: string, message: string, meta?: Record<string, unknown>): void {

   112→

    43→ * Records LLM duration histogram and token counters for a completed call.
    44→ * Safe to call even when no MeterProvider is registered (instruments are no-ops).
    45→ */
    46→export function recordLlmMetrics(

The tests use dynamic `import()` which means the module is cached after the first import. Since `logs.getLogger("brain-server")` is called inside `emitLogRecord`, the provider set in `beforeAll` should work. But the issue is likely that the module is cached from a previous test file import before the provider is set up.

1. **`ai-telemetry.ts`** — `TokenUsage` is now an alias for `LanguageModelUsage` from the AI SDK (which renamed `promptTokens`/`completionTokens` to `inputTokens`/`outputTokens` in v6). Updated `recordLlmMetrics` to use the new property names.

> AGENT

The `telemetry-init.test.ts` calls `initTelemetry()` which sets its own global `LoggerProvider`, overwriting the one set by the logger test's `beforeAll`. In CI (Bun 1.3.10), these may share a process. Fix: use `beforeEach` to reset the provider before each test.

> TOOL

  "new_string": "import { describe, test, expect, beforeEach, afterAll } from \"bun:test\";\nimport { logs, SeverityNumber } from \"@opentelemetry/api-logs\";\nimport { LoggerProvider, SimpleLogRecordProcessor, InMemoryLogRecordExporter } from \"@opentelemetry/sdk-logs\";\n\ndescribe(\"telemetry/logger\", () => {\n  const exporter = new InMemoryLogRecordExporter();\n  let originalProvider: ReturnType<typeof logs.getLoggerProvider>;\n\n  beforeEach(() => {\n    originalProvider = logs.getLoggerProvider();\n    const provider = new LoggerProvider({\n      processors: [new SimpleLogRecordProcessor(exporter)],\n    });\n    logs.setGlobalLoggerProvider(provider);\n    exporter.getFinishedLogRecords().length = 0;\n  });\n\n  afterAll(() => {\n    logs.setGlobalLoggerProvider(originalProvider);\n  });\n\n  test(\"log.info emits OTEL log record with INFO severity\", async () => {\n    const { log } = await import(\"../../app/src/server/telemetry/logger\");"

The fix: clear the global key before setting our provider. Let me find the key name.

> AGENT

Pushed `69ed5d00`. The root cause: `@opentelemetry/api-logs`'s `setGlobalLoggerProvider` silently no-ops if the global key (`Symbol.for('io.opentelemetry.js.api.logs')`) already exists on `globalThis`. In CI, `initTelemetry()` from `telemetry-init.test.ts` registers first (same process), so the logger test's provider was never actually set. The fix deletes the global symbol key before each test to force re-registration.
